One: it is judged (yuqda), said by al-Dahhak.

The second: it is written (yuktab), said by Ibn Abbas.

The third: it descends (yanzil), said by Ibn Zayd.

The fourth: it comes forth (yakhruj), said by Ibn Sinan.

Regarding the interpretation of ﴿every wise matter﴾ there are four aspects:

One: the terms of life, provision, happiness and misery, from year to year; said by Ibn Abbas.

The second: everything that is decreed from year to year, except happiness and misery, for these are in the Mother of the Book and are not changed or altered; said by Ibn Umar.

The third: everything that is decreed from year to year except life and death; said by Mujahid.

The Night of Power remains as long as time endures, and it is in the month of Ramadan (p-246) within its last ten nights.

There is disagreement about its place within the last ten nights of Ramadan, with several opinions which he mentioned in the Surah of al-Qadr, which is more appropriate.

One of them: that the command is the Qur'an which Allah sent down from Him; related by al-Naqqash.

The second: that it is what Allah decreed in the blessed night concerning the conditions of His servants; said by Ibn Isa.

It may also mean, as a third aspect: the sending of Muhammad ﷺ as a prophet.

﴿Indeed, We are ever sending﴾. Regarding this there are three aspects:

One: sending the messengers as warners.

The second: sending down what We have decreed upon the servants.

The third: sending as a mercy from your Lord.

Regarding ﴿a mercy from your Lord﴾ here there are two aspects:

One: that it is Allah's blessing in sending His Messenger ﷺ.

The second: that it is His compassion in guiding those who believe in him.

Regarding His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿on the day when the sky will bring a visible smoke﴾, there are three opinions:

His saying, Exalted and Majestic is He: ﴿Our Lord, remove the punishment from us; indeed we are believers﴾. Regarding this there are three opinions:

One of them: that it is the smoke. This was said by Qatadah.

The second: the hunger. This was said by al-Naqqash.

The third: that it is the snow. This has no basis, because this would be either in the Hereafter or regarding the people of Makkah, and Makkah was not among the lands of snow. However, it has been related, so we have recorded it.

One of them: that is, they will return to the Fire of Jahannam.

The second: to polytheism. This was said by Ibn Mas'ud.

The second: the punishment of Jahannam on the Day of Resurrection. This was said by Ibn 'Abbas and al-Hasan.

Two: with a plain proof; said by Yahya.

It is as if he said: "If you are truthful about their restoration for recompense, then restore them for obligation."

This is like the saying of one who says: "If there are going to arise after us a people of sons, then why does not the one who has passed of the fathers return?"

His statement, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿Are they better, or the people of Tubba'?﴾ Concerning this there are two views:

The first: Are they superior in visible blessing and greater in wealth?

The second: Are they more honored and mightier than the people of Tubba'?

Qatadah related that Tubba' was a man from Himyar who marched with armies until he crossed al-Hirah and reached Samarqand, and destroyed it.

It has been related to us that when he wrote, he would write in the name of Allah, who raised high and possessed land, sea, morning light and wind.

It was narrated from Amr ibn Raja' from Sahl ibn Sa'd al-Sa'idi that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Do not revile Tubba', for he had embraced Islam."

Regarding his being named Tubba' there are two views:

The first: because he followed (tabi'a) those before him among the kings of Yemen, just as it is said khalifah (successor) because he succeeded (khalafa) those before him.

The second: because it is a title for the kings of Yemen.

Allah censured his people but did not censure him, and He cited them as an example for Quraysh, because of their nearness to their dwelling, and because of their greatness in their souls. His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿Indeed, the tree of al-Zaqqum﴾ ﴿is the food of the sinful.﴾ We have already mentioned the various opinions concerning al-Zaqqum. Linguistically, it means what is eaten with great aversion.

For this reason it is said: "He tazaqqama this food," meaning he ate it with great aversion, as one who stuffs his mouth out of extreme distaste.

Al-Naqqash related from Mujahid that the tree of al-Zaqqum is Abu Jahl.

Regarding al-Atheem (the sinful), there are two views:
One: it is the sinner, as said by Ibn Isa.
The second: it is the polytheist who acquires sin, as said by Yahya.

His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿Seize him and drag him﴾ has five interpretations:
First: then drag him, as said by al-Hasan.
Second: then push him, as said by Mujahid.
Third: then drive him, related by al-Kalbi.
Fourth: then break him as wood is broken, related by al-A'mash.
Fifth: then force him back violently, as said by Ibn Qutayba.

al-Farazdaq said:
"The noble are not those who give their fathers to you as a pledge, until you return to 'Atiyya, who is dragged along."

One: the middle of the Fire, as said by Ibn Abbas, al-Dahhak and Qatada.
The second: the greater part of the Fire, where the heat strikes him from all its sides, as said by al-Hasan.

**Commentary of al-Mawardi (al-Nukat wa al-Uyun) on surah 44, verses 51–59:**

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, the righteous will be in a secure place﴾. On this there are three interpretations:

First: secure from Satan and from sorrows. This is the view of Qatadah.

Second: secure from punishment. This is the view of al-Kalbi.

Third: secure from death. This is the view of Muqatil.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿They will wear fine silk and thick brocade﴾. On these two words there are three interpretations:

First: al-sundus (السُّنْدُس) is thin silk, and al-istabraq (الإسْتَبْرَق) is thick brocade. This is the view of Ikrimah.

Second: al-sundus is woven in the markets of Iraq and is the finest embroidery. This is the view of Yahya. Al-istabraq is brocade, and it was named istabraq for the intensity of its shine (barq). This is the view of al-Zajjaj.

Third: al-sundus is what they wear, and al-istabraq is what they spread out as bedding.

Regarding ﴿facing one another﴾ (مُتَقابِلِينَ), there are two interpretations: (p-259)
First: facing one another in love, not turning their backs on one another in hatred. This is the view of Ali ibn Isa.

Second: facing one another in their gatherings, so that no one looks at the back of another. This is the view of Mujahid.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So We have made it easy with your tongue﴾, meaning the Qur'an. On this there are two interpretations:

First: its meaning is that We made it Arabic on your tongue.

Second: its meaning is that We loosened your tongue for it, as facilitation.

﴿So that they may remember﴾ admits of two interpretations:

First: that they may return (to the truth).

Second: that they may take heed.

﴿So wait, and indeed they are waiting﴾. On this there are two interpretations:

First: wait for what I have promised you of victory over them. Al-Naqqash related that it means: they are waiting for your death.

Second: wait for what I have promised you of reward, for they are among those awaiting what You have promised them of punishment. And Allah knows best.
